title: Symmetry and Geometric Classification of an Odd Rational Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
question: Determine whether the function f(x) = \frac{x^5 - 3x}{x^4 + 1} is even, odd, or neither, and identify the geometric symmetry of its graph.

options.text: Odd function with symmetry with respect to the origin
options.explanation: Correct! Evaluating f(-x) gives [(-x)^5 - 3(-x)] / [(-x)^4 + 1] = [-x^5 + 3x] / [x^4 + 1] = -f(x). Since f(-x) = -f(x), the function is odd and its graph is symmetric with respect to the origin.

options.text: Even function with symmetry with respect to the y-axis
options.explanation: Incorrect. An even function requires f(-x) = f(x), but here the sign of the numerator is negated.
options.misconception: Student observes the constant +1 in the denominator and erroneously concludes that any function containing even constant terms must possess even parity.

options.text: Odd function with symmetry with respect to the y-axis
options.explanation: Incorrect. Odd functions exhibit origin symmetry, not y-axis symmetry.
options.misconception: Student correctly identifies the odd algebraic parity condition f(-x) = -f(x) but confuses geometric symmetries, assigning y-axis reflection symmetry to an odd function instead of origin rotation.

options.text: Neither even nor odd with no symmetry
options.explanation: Incorrect. The function satisfies the exact algebraic identity for odd symmetry f(-x) = -f(x).
options.misconception: Student fails to factor out the negative sign from the numerator, concluding that -x^5 + 3x is unrelated to x^5 - 3x and therefore possesses no symmetry.

explanation: We test f(-x) = [(-x)^5 - 3(-x)] / [(-x)^4 + 1] = [-x^5 + 3x] / [x^4 + 1] = -[(x^5 - 3x) / (x^4 + 1)] = -f(x). Because f(-x) = -f(x) for all real x, f is an odd function. The graph of an odd function possesses 180-degree rotational symmetry with respect to the origin.
